claims.text: Atomic-size mismatches produce inherent local lattice distortions in HfNbTaTiZr.
Heating HfNbTaTiZr activates additional local lattice distortions and lattice relaxations.
Increasing temperature enhances atomic mobility in HfNbTaTiZr.
Thermally activated lattice distortions alter dislocation behavior.
Elevated temperature shifts the dominant dislocation mechanism at least partly from glide toward climb.
Elevated temperature activates additional slip systems in HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed change in dislocation behavior reduces the alloy's yield strength.
The proposed thermally activated mechanism reduces the alloy's elastic modulus.
The proposed mechanism causes thermal expansion to deviate from a simple low-temperature extrapolation.
Between approximately 600 and 900 degrees Celsius, yield strength will be statistically significantly lower than at room temperature.
Between approximately 600 and 900 degrees Celsius, elastic modulus will be statistically significantly lower than at room temperature.
Between approximately 600 and 900 degrees Celsius, thermal expansion will deviate from simple extrapolations of low-temperature behavior.
Microstructural characterization after or during elevated-temperature testing will reveal altered dislocation mechanisms.
Microstructural characterization will reveal increased lattice distortion at elevated temperature.
At room temperature or below approximately 600 degrees Celsius, dislocation glide dominates.
At room temperature or below approximately 600 degrees Celsius, lattice distortions are minimal.
Below approximately 500 degrees Celsius thermal activation is too low for the proposed behavior, while above approximately 1000 degrees Celsius oxidation or phase changes may dominate.
